newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia court tells town to remove Albanian flag.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia court tells town to remove Albanian flag.

text.p: Macedonia's constitutional court on Wednesday ordered the removal of an Albanian flag hoisted outside a town hall at the centre of simmering tension between ethnic Albanians and Macedonians.

The ethnic Albanian PDPA Party in Gostivar, a mostly Albanian town in the west of Macedonia, hoisted the flag in February after winning a local election. It also hoisted the Turkish flag in solidarity with Macedonia's Turkish minority.
The move outraged ethnic Macedonians, who saw it is an expression of a desire to split the country along ethnic lines, and several political parties went to the constitutional court.
Court president Milan Netkov said the flags of foreign countries could be hoisted only under strictly determined conditions.
"Neither Albania nor Turkey has the mandate to rule over Gostivar," he said.

Macedonia's ethnic Albanian parties are increasingly demanding constitutional recognition for the Albanians, who account for 23 percent of Macedonia's population of two million, according to an official census.

Gostivar mayor Ruffi Osmani struck a defiant note, saying: "I would not advise the government to implement the constitutional court decision by force... The Albanian flag is the national symbol of Albanians wherever they are."
At least 5,000 Albanians have demonstrated twice in Gostivar in the past month, waving the Albanian national flag and singing the Albanian national anthem, prompting scuffles with ethnic Macedonians.
